ANSWER: Approximately 13.8% (19 out of 138) of README.md files belonging to repositories that do not use Python include copyright information.

METHOD:
1. From the artifacts_database `contents` table, I selected all files whose path is exactly "README.md" (case-insensitive) or ends with "/README.md" — 204 README.md files across 200 repositories.
2. I joined these repositories to the metadata_database `languages` table (178 of the 200 repos had language metadata; 22 were unmatched and excluded). A repository was classified as "does not use Python" if its language_description does not mention "Python" (case-insensitive). Repos with "No language information available" were treated as non-Python (Python is not among their declared languages). This yielded 138 README.md files in non-Python repositories (44 README files belonged to Python-using repos).
3. A README was deemed to include copyright information if its content contained the word "copyright" (case-insensitive) or the © symbol: 19 of 138 files matched → 19/138 ≈ 13.8%.

ROBUSTNESS CHECKS:
- Requiring the literal word "copyright" only (no © symbol): 17/138 ≈ 12.3%.
- Also counting bare "(c)" notices: 21/138 ≈ 15.2%.
- Restricting to repos with explicit (non-"No language information") language metadata: 19/130 ≈ 14.6%.
- Repo-level (≥1 README with copyright per repo): 19/135 ≈ 14.1%.

All variants cluster around 12–15%; the headline figure is ≈13.8% (about one in seven).
